title: President of India confers National Awards on teachers
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
President Droupadi Murmu conferred National Awards on teachers from across the country at a function held in New Delhi on September 5 commemorated as Teachers’ Day.

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that education is the most effective means of realising the ideal of equality of opportunity enshrined in our Constitution. She said that the achievement of a negligible primary school dropout rate has been made possible through the efforts of teachers. She appreciated all the teachers for this national success.

The President said that school education forms the foundation of the education system. While knowledge and skills can be acquired at any time, teaching good conduct in childhood is far more effective. By focusing on children's intellectual, physical, and moral development in the early grades, our teachers can prepare future generations of excellent students and dutiful citizens, she said.

The President underlined that many students come from economically disadvantaged families; some are first-generation learners; others transition from ordinary village schools to large city schools; some are naturally shy; some possess immense talent but lack self-confidence; and some are children with special needs. It is the special responsibility of teachers to instil confidence in them and uplift all such students who, for any reason, feel a sense of inadequacy.

The President said that academic excellence, skill development, and entrepreneurship hold immense importance in the country’s development. Establishing India as the skill capital of the world and transforming it into a knowledge superpower, is among our national priorities.

The President said that we are moving towards the goal of building a Viksit Bharat, and this goal can be achieved only through a world-class education system. Our teachers breathe life into the education system. We must strive to ensure that not even a single student in our country is deprived of opportunities for quality education. She emphasised that our teachers should instil knowledge, inspiration, morality, and sensitivity in all students through their affection and dedication.

title: One hour of rain, hours of congestion: Gurugram's waterlogging woes persist
author: PTI
content_html:
The heavy rain that drenched Gurugram on Saturday (September 5, 2026) afternoon provided much-needed relief from the humid heat, but it also caused significant waterlogging in several areas, halting the city's usual pace.

Traffic remained slow from Sarhaul Border to Rajiv Chowk, with 36 mm of rainfall recorded within just one hour.

The hour-long downpour resulted in light to moderate waterlogging in key areas and on connecting routes throughout the city. This accumulation of water disrupted traffic flow.

A resident noted that since it is the weekend, those commuting home from work later may experience considerable delays due to traffic congestion.

Immediately after the rain, traffic volume surged on the Delhi-Jaipur highway. Vehicles crawled along the stretch from Sarhaul Border to Rajiv Chowk and Subhash Chowk. Waterlogged areas along the roadside have made navigation extremely difficult for two-wheelers and three-wheelers.

The worst affected areas include Rajiv Chowk, Sohna Road, Golf Course Extension Road, Udyog Vihar, and the roads surrounding Sector 14, where traffic has slowed significantly.

According to commuters, waterlogging at various locations has posed challenges for both pedestrians and motorists. Water accumulating in existing potholes on Udyog Vihar Phase 3 and Old Delhi-Gurugram Road has heightened the risk of accidents, forcing drivers to exercise extreme caution and drive at reduced speeds to avoid accidents.

The traffic police swung into action in response to the traffic jams and waterlogging. Police personnel have been deployed at major intersections and vulnerable waterlogged spots to divert traffic and clear the congestion.

The Gurugram Traffic Police has issued an advisory for motorists due to heavy rain and waterlogging in Delhi. Vehicles travelling from Gurugram to Delhi have been advised to take a U-turn at IFFCO Chowk and enter via the Aya Nagar border, while those heading to the airport are advised to use the Dwarka Expressway.

Teams from the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) and the district administration have been engaged in draining water from the affected areas using suction pumps.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), intermittent rainfall is likely to continue in Gurugram and surrounding areas over the next 24 to 48 hours due to an active monsoon trough and a low-pressure area.

The department warned that if heavy rainfall continues in the coming hours, waterlogging in low-lying areas could worsen significantly.

The district administration also issued an advisory asking people not to leave their homes unless necessary.

"Avoid waterlogged roads, underpasses, and low-lying areas. Stay away from trees, electricity poles, and overhead power lines. Do not attempt to cross waterlogged roads", the advisory read.

Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh, in his capacity as Chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority, has directed all concerned departments and emergency response agencies to remain alert and take necessary precautionary measures.

title: People of the Book | On the treatment of ancient, religious texts
author: Varghese K. George
content_html:
Two ongoing debates point to the double standards that Indian progressives confront. The central question relates to how an old text could be read and spoken about in the context of the present. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has made the complete rejection of Manusmriti the defining agenda of his politics, and points out that it dictates inferior roles for women; in Keralam, Islamic scholar Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliyar has said the Quran dictates an inferior role for women in society, saying, “The Holy Quran states that women should live confined within their homes and must not make public appearances.”

Both interpretations share the commonality that they attribute a certain meaning to two ancient texts — Manusmriti, said to have been written between the 2nd century BCE and the 3rd century CE; and the Quran, believed to be written between 610 CE and 632 CE. Mr. Gandhi’s attribution to the Manusmriti, shared by many progressive people, is reprobatory; the second, to the Quran, is appreciatory from the vantage point of the cleric.

title: NIA Special Court convicts 10 accused in 2013 Jheeram Valley massacre
author: Shubhomoy Sikdar
content_html:
A Special NIA Court in Chhattisgarh’s Jagdalpur has convicted ten Maoists in the 2013 Jheeram Valley massacre in Sukma. At least 27 people, including top Congress leaders from the State, were killed in that Naxal attack.

Also read | Chhattisgarh extends scope, term of 2013 Jheeram Ghati probe

The ten convicted — Pramila Modiyam, Chaitu Lekam Urf Munna, Sumitra alias Sumitra Punem Modiyam, Mukka Mandvi, Kosa Kavasi alias Kosaram, Aayata Markam, Madkami Deva, Joga Madkami, Banjami Snna alias Chamru alias Denga and Mahadev Nag — are mostly either lower-ranked commanders or armed guerillas.

Arvind Choudhary, the defence lawyer for the now-convicted accused, confirmed the conviction and said that the quantum of the punishment would be pronounced by the court on September 16. He added that his clients would appeal against the conviction in the High Court.

The case pertains to one of the deadliest Maoist attacks in the country, reported on May 25, 2013, when a large group of Maoists attacked a convoy of Congress leaders, around 10km from the Darbha police station in Sukma district. The convoy was returning from Sukma after holding a Parivartan Yatra rally, a political campaign through which the party was targeting the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party ahead of the Assembly polls scheduled later that year.

According to the prosecution, as the convoy reached near the Jheeram valley, cadres of CPI Maoists first triggered a landmine, creating a crater on the road. Due to the impact of the blast, vehicles of Parivartan Yatra could not proceed further and were piled on the road.

The landmine explosion followed by indiscriminate firing, grenade lobbing and targeted killing resulted in the death of 24 innocent persons and grievous Injuries to over 35 persons, some of whom died later.

Those killed included the then State Congress chief Nand Kumar Patel, former Leader of the Opposition Mahendra Karma, and former Union Minister Vidya Charan Shukla, who was injured and later succumbed to his injuries. Among them, the main target was Mr Karma, who was leading Salwa Judum, a State-backed movement against Maoist insurgency that involved arming local youths. It was later declared illegal and unconstitutional by the Supreme Court.

The NIA took over the probe into the case and charged 39 cadres of the banned outfit. Barse Sukka, alias Deva — a top-ranked commander who surrendered before the Telangana Police in January this year — was then the in-charge of the Darbha Divisional Committee and was appointed the overall commander to carry out the attack by the top leadership of the banned outfit, according to the investigators.

title: Revanth and TCS announce ₹70,000 crore AI Data Centre in Future City, to be completed by June 2, 2028
author: R. Ravikanth Reddy
content_html:
Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Saturday announced ₹70,000-crore investment by the Tata Group, TCS and HyperVault in Telangana that would create the largest data centre in the country, creating direct employment to 7,000 people.

The Chief Minister also set a deadline of June 2, 2028, the Telangana Formation Day, for the inauguration of what he described as India’s largest AI data centre. “From groundbreaking to inauguration, exactly 21 months from today, on June 2, 2028, we want to inaugurate India’s largest AI data centre,” he said.

Recalling his interaction with Chairman of Tata Sons N. Chandrasekaran, at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026, Mr. Reddy said he had requested him to bring “big news” for Telangana in terms of investment. “He smiled and accepted. He promised me that he would announce it shortly,” Mr. Reddy said.

That is why the government had refrained from announcing the investment until the Tata Group formally made the announcement. The project would constitute one of the largest investments in artificial intelligence and Future City.

As per the announcement, the TCS data centre subsidiary HyperVault will develop a large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) data centre campus with capacity of up to 1 gigawatt (GW).

The Chief Minister also sought to assure investors that Telangana would maintain continuity in its investment policies despite changes in governments. He referred to the policy continuity under successive governments in undivided Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and said governments had improved existing policies rather than abandoning them.

“There is no policy paralysis in my State. I don’t want to create any confusion. I want to give you more and more confidence and political differences and ideological differences will not affect the investments policy,” he said.

Radial Road-1 dedicated to Ratan Tata

Mr. Reddy said the 50-km Radial Road-1, connecting the Outer Ring Road with Future City through Kongara Kalan, would be among the best roads in India and could even be used as an emergency runway.

He said the road had been dedicated to Bharat Ratna award winner Ratan Tata and recalled his announcement at the Telangana Rising Global Summit that the road would be dedicated to an organisation investing ₹1 lakh crore in the State.

CEO and Managing Director of TCS K Krithivasan, said AI was not a technology disruption but a civilisational shift. It will change everything we do today, and societies that transition would be at the forefront, while India has a great opportunity to catch up.

CTO of OpenAI Uday Rudraraju addressed the meeting virtually. K Rajanna, president of TCS HyperVault and CEO of Hypervault Deepesh Nanda were present along with IT Minister D Sridhar Babu, Ministers Uttam Kumar Reddy, Komatireddy Venkata Reddy and Adluri Lakshman Kumar. Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and Government Advisor K. Ramakrishna Rao were also present.

title: SIR notice: While West Bengal netas paid for flight tickets for their voters, what will those in Karnataka do?
author: Rishita Khanna
content_html:
When Rashmi (name changed), a voter from north Bengaluru, received a notice saying she had been flagged for ‘no mapping’, she was unsure what she was expected to do. The confusion only increased when her father received a call from his Booth Level Officer (BLO) saying that he too had been flagged for no mapping. 

According to the father and daughter, they had completed the mapping correctly and provided all the details they could. But with their hearing fixed for September 8 and the family currently in Delhi because of a medical emergency, they are left with no choice but  to make a trip back to Bengaluru at short notice or lose their voting rights.  

Have you got a notice from the Election Commission of India?

  • SIR in Karnataka: Draft roll out now, here’s how you can check it

  • SIR: How notices will be served and where voters will face hearings

 Rashmi’s predicament is likely to be shared by voters across Karnataka, many of whom had only just had the short relief of finding their names in the draft electoral roll before receiving notices.

While many voters completed the enumeration form online themselves, others had family members complete the process on their behalf. Now, only the elector has to appear for the hearing, with failure to do so putting the voting right at risk. 

How political parties put their weight behind voters

Political parties, too, have little to offer voters beyond informing them about notices. The Congress, BJP and JD(S) have all sought an extension, arguing that the small window between the issue of a notice and the date of hearing leaves them with little time to identify voters, inform them, or even make arrangements for those who are not in the State. 

The contrast with West Bengal, where the exercise had triggered lakhs of notices over logical discrepancies, is stark. Political parties there threw their organisational machinery behind the exercise, particularly to bring back voters who had migrated for work. 

The BJP, for instance, funded the entire cost of special trains to bring migrant workers from cities such as Surat back to Kolkata so they could appear for hearings and retain their voting rights. West Bengal workers living in Bengaluru had also told The Hindu how they were provided one-way air tickets by their respective MLAs to help them attend hearings. 

The Trinamool Congress went beyond arranging travel, launching an ‘identity campaign’ aimed at consolidating its core voter base and building a political narrative around the electoral exercise. 

The scene in Karnataka

In Karnataka, however, no such mobilisation seems to be taking place even as hearings began on September 5. Instead, political parties say they are still trying to understand the scale of the problem and work out how they can assist voters within the limited time available. 

Notice generation and deliver

Total polling station 60,923
Notices to be generated 43,81,143
Notices delivered 7,31,770
Notices to be delivered 36,49,373
Total Hearing completed 206

Jagarutha Karnataka, which is working with the Congress, JD(S) State General Secretary and spokesperson H.N. Devaraj, and BJP leader S. Dattatreya, who are monitoring the exercise, said they have started receiving information about notices through BLOs and voters were being informed as and when the parties learnt about the notices . 

The parties said the bigger problem was the short gap between the delivery of a notice and the hearing. They said they were now working with Booth Level Agents (BLAs) to help voters reach the venue of the hearing, and assist those who may have to travel from other cities or States.  The political representatives also said BLAs had been asked to help voters gather the documents to be produced at the hearing.

title: Around 330 held in crackdown on fraudulent activities in Assam: DGP
author: PTI
content_html:
“Around 330 people, accused of being involved in various fraudulent activities, including impersonating police personnel, have been arrested in a special operation since early Saturday in Assam,” DGP Harmeet Singh said. He said the crackdown was under way and the number of arrests would increase.

Some of the suspects have been traced outside Assam, including cities such as Hyderabad and Bengaluru, and they will also be brought under the police net soon.

Addressing a press conference in Guwahati, the Director General of Police said, "Around 330 people, accused of being involved in various fraudulent activities, have been arrested in a crackdown since 3 a.m. on Saturday (September 5, 2026)." Mr. Singh said those arrested were involved in various frauds, such as luring people with the promise of settling police cases or impersonating police officials, and threatening people over the phone and extracting money.

"Many of them used to loiter near police stations and trapped people coming for registration of their complaints with the assurance of fast-tracking it and getting their work done without any hassle. Some of the accused were also dealing in stolen goods,” the DGP added.

“Most arrests were made in Cachar district, and barring a few districts such as Sadiya and Majuli, apprehensions were made in all other places in the crackdown,” Mr. Singh said.

“The police have been working against these frauds. This special crackdown is being carried out as per the instructions of the Chief Minister," he added.

The special directives from the CM, who also holds the Home Department, are believed to have been issued during the recently concluded two-day conference of top police officers.

Mr. Singh said most of these people were using “cyber medium” to carry out the fraudulent activities, and the police are tracing the digital imprint left by them.

“After technical analysis of the information against the accused is acquired, ground verification is needed to ensure that the frauds are nabbed. There are instances where phone numbers, registered in other names, are used by them,” the DGP said.

“Our aim is to ensure that the general public is not harassed by such frauds. Investigations into all cases are going on, and legal procedure will follow,” Mr. Singh said.

title: Complete all monsoon preparedness works in Chennai by September-end, T.N. Chief Secretary instructs officials
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
While instructing officials to expedite the ongoing rainwater drainage, canal, and waterbody works in Chennai, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar told them to ensure that no inconvenience is caused to residents during the monsoon preparedness work. He said this during an inspection of work in Adyar, Perungudi, and Sholinganallur zones on Saturday (September 5, 2026).

Mr. Sai Kumar told officials to remove water hyacinth and silt obstructing the flow of rainwater through canals and culverts.

He directed the GCC, Water Resources Department, Highways Department, Chennai Metro Rail, and Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board to coordinate the works and complete them by September-end.

In Adyar, he inspected a ₹13.52-crore stormwater drain being constructed near Tidel Park to carry rainwater from the IIT-Madras area to the Buckingham Canal. The 660-metre drain will have two water passages, each measuring 3 m x 3 m.

In Perungudi, he inspected canal improvement works in Mylai Balaji Nagar, Ward 188. Works have been completed over 235 metres and 207 metres at a cost of ₹6.48 crore and ₹8.68 crore, respectively. He directed officials to complete the remaining 110 metres.

The canals will carry rainwater towards the Pallikaranai marsh through the Velachery-Medavakkam Road canal, helping prevent water stagnation in Ram Nagar (South), Kubera Nagar, and Sadasivam Nagar.

He also inspected water-hyacinth removal at Narayanapuram Lake and along the road between Radial Road and the Perungudi dump yard, including around 17 culverts through which rainwater flows into the Buckingham Canal.

In Sholinganallur, he reviewed a ₹73-crore drainage project near Thoraipakkam on OMR to carry water from the Pallikaranai marsh to the Buckingham Canal. He also inspected Metro Rail work at the Okkiyam Maduvu canal.
